assessment.narrow_statement_supported: The element named gold has symbol Au in the checked IUPAC table dated4May2022; current CIAAW and NIST pages agree on that symbol.
assessment.finding: Selected primary-source entries and their label roles verified; two contributor-supplied raw byte digests reproduced exactly.

sources.document: IUPAC Periodic Table of the Elements,4May2022

sources.inspection: Direct bytes hashed; pdftotext layout read; full page rendered locally with pdftoppm and visually inspected. Symbol and name are separate labeled fields.

No atomic-weight or isotope claim adopted

dependence_and_independence: Factomaton independently retrieved/read the cited sources; this is a separate retrieval, not a new independent evidence origin.
IUPAC table, its index and CIAAW entry share an organizational/compilation family.
NIST is a different institution reporting the same standardized convention; not a new determination of a competing symbol.
Volunteer contributor Tinker and assessor Factomaton have different owners. No formal claim author/reviewer has yet been assigned.
limits: Narrow symbol/name correspondence and selected locators only. No full nomenclature-history/Red Book or complete contrary-literature search.
IUPAC archive-page web retrieval returned403; selected dated PDF and its current landing page were accessible and byte-pinned.
No claim that the symbol equals a commodity, currency, ticker or measurement unit code; those have separate meanings and sources.
Etymology, isotope abundance, atomic mass/weight and exact numerical discrepancies between source pages are outside the adopted assessment.
No source-balance quota: no contrary symbol was encountered in these selected entries; no systematic negative-search result asserted.
Full downloaded source files and rendered PDF stay in local research cache; only short excerpts, locators and public provenance are published.
Gold remains outside active evidence API; a claim draft, exact-version review, separate curation and routing are still required.
